questions.q: Why does network latency make synchronous replication impractical over real geographic distance, per this lesson?
options: The primary must wait for confirmation from the secondary, and that round-trip is bounded by the physical speed of light over fiber, adding real delay to every commit as distance grows
Synchronous replication is a licensing feature not available over long distances
Network latency only affects asynchronous replication, not synchronous
Distance has no measurable effect on replication performance
questions.explain: Synchronous replication requires waiting for the secondary's confirmation, and that round-trip delay grows with real physical distance.

questions.q: What does a close DR site provide, and what doesn't it protect against, per this lesson?
options: Low latency and near-zero RPO via synchronous replication, but no protection against a disaster affecting the entire region
Protection against regional disasters but with poor performance
Nothing useful — close DR sites provide no real benefit
Guaranteed protection against every possible disaster type
questions.explain: A close site enables synchronous replication and low RPO, but shares regional risk with the primary, so it can't survive a region-wide event.

questions.q: What does a distant DR site force, per this lesson?
options: Asynchronous replication, accepting a non-zero RPO, in exchange for genuine protection against a regional disaster
Synchronous replication with zero data loss, with no downsides
The elimination of the need for any RPO/RTO targets
Automatic conversion to transactional replication
questions.explain: The distance needed to escape shared regional risk is the same distance that makes synchronous replication impractical, forcing async and a non-zero RPO.

questions.q: How can data residency requirements affect geographic DR site selection, per this lesson?
options: They can legally constrain where a DR site is allowed to exist, sometimes forcing a closer, same-jurisdiction option over a more protective distant one
Data residency requirements have no bearing on DR site location
Data residency only applies to backup files, never to live replicas
Data residency requirements always favor the most distant possible site
questions.explain: Regulatory or contractual data residency requirements can restrict DR site location regardless of what would otherwise be the best technical choice.

questions.q: Why can't a company get both a DR site 'far enough to survive a regional disaster' and zero-data-loss synchronous replication to it, per this lesson?
options: That combination is blocked by network physics — real distance adds latency that makes synchronous replication impractical, so it's a tradeoff, not a configuration choice
It's entirely possible with the right SQL Server edition
This is a licensing restriction that can be removed with the right settings
Synchronous replication doesn't depend on distance at all
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes this is a physical tradeoff (latency vs. distance), not something a product setting can override.
